title: The Executioner and Her Way of Life
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a world where people summoned from Japan, the 'Lost Ones', are linked to catastrophes, the young priestess and Executioner Menou is tasked with killing them. When a Japanese girl named Akari, whose time power seems to make her unkillable, insists on travelling with her, Menou sets off to find a way to end her (Yen Press blurb via AniList/MU; ANN Manga Guide).
life_message: Duty to an institution collides with personal bonds, and a killer may have to question the mission she was raised for.

content.note: Menou's group 'resort to stabbing first, asking questions never' (ANN); assassination of summoned teens (blurb); AniList Assassins, MU Murder/s.
Dark early twist that subverts isekai (ANN); catastrophic powers (blurb).
Yuri undertones (AniList Yuri 71, MU Shoujo Ai); obsessive character (MU).

dominant: Killing for the greater good; a religious order's authority; bond between killer and target

frames.aligns: Questions killing innocents for an institution's ends.
frames.concerns: A priestess-assassin; religious order shown sanctioning murder of strangers.

frames.aligns: Killing shown as weighty, not casual, in the premise.
frames.concerns: Clergy as executioners; mockery of holy office possible (to verify).

frames.aligns: Bond with Akari may humanize Menou.

frames.concerns: Magic and a church as assassin guild.

frames.aligns: Two kingdoms: misuse of spiritual office for the sword.

frames.concerns: Violence; yuri undertones for holiness churches.

frames.aligns: Moral complexity about duty and killing.
Critique of institutions that kill outsiders.

frames.concerns: First precept broken by the heroine's job.

frames.aligns: Female-led; critique of xenophobic killing of outsiders.
Immortality theme touches life over death.
Righteous duty vs killing the innocent.

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Killings are duty, not personal honor (blurb).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Religious order directs Menou's duty (MU Priestess/es, Executioner/s).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Mission for the world against Lost Ones (blurb).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Religious order and doctrine govern society (AniList Religion).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Survival against catastrophe drives the mission (blurb).

folkways.japan: Turns the Japanese isekai convention around, treating Japanese visitors as dangerous outsiders; Menou's self-effacing duty echoes Japanese role loyalty.

delivery.evidence: ANN reviewers discuss twist and pacing, not messaging (to verify).

personified.ideology: Duty to the order: killing outsiders for the world's safety

delivery.note: The killing mission is the heroine's own view, so the story examines it from inside.

winners_losers: Menou and Akari hold the reader's sympathy; the institution that sends executioners is a question mark in volume 1.
to_verify: How the religious order is portrayed in later volumes.
